content: Wolframin is a protein encoded by the WFS1 gene in humans. Wolframin is classified as a transmembrane protein. It is believed to function as a cation-selective ion channel, facilitating the movement of positively charged ions across cellular membranes. Mutations in the WFS1 gene are linked to an autosomal recessive syndrome that manifests with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and bilateral progressive optic atrophy. These symptoms typically present during childhood or early adulthood. This syndrome may also involve a range of neurological symptoms, including an increased susceptibility to psychiatric disorders. A significant number and variety of mutations in the WFS1 gene, particularly those occurring in exon 8, are associated with this syndrome. Additionally, mutations in the WFS1 gene can lead to autosomal dominant deafness 6 (DFNA6), which is also referred to as DFNA14 or DFNA38. Mutations in this gene have also been implicated in the development of congenital cataracts.
